transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep hearing voices, and it’s gotten to where I can’t just brush it off anymore. It’s not like a thought in my head, you know? It’s clear, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio apartment with me. I’ll be sitting there and the house is quiet, nobody’s there, and I hear someone say my name. Sometimes it’s just my name, real plain, and other times it’s like they’re telling me my work is being judged.

And I try to check—like I’ll look around, turn things down, listen at the door, because I think maybe it’s a neighbor or somebody outside, but then there’s nobody. It feels so real that it makes me nervous, and I don’t know what to do with it anymore. That’s why I’m here.
What kind of things do the voices usually say to you, are they ever telling you to do something?

Mostly they say my name, like real clear, like somebody is right there in the room with me. It’ll be quiet in my studio, no TV on or anything, and I’ll hear it—my name—plain as day. And I’ll stop what I’m doing and look around, because it doesn’t feel like it’s coming from inside me, it feels like somebody standing there saying it.

Other times it’s more like they’re talking about me, like saying my work is being judged, like I’m being watched or graded somehow. That one gets to me because I work hard, you know, and then I start wondering what they mean by that, who’s judging it, why they’re saying it. It makes me nervous and I’ll check around, listen, try to figure out where it’s coming from.

As far as telling me to do something… I don’t know, not like giving me clear orders that I can remember. It’s more the name and the judging comments that keep happening.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something or influence what actions you take?

I wouldn’t say they tell me, like, “go do this” in a direct way… not like a clear command that I have to follow. But they do affect what I do, because when I hear it, I stop everything. I’ll be in my little studio and the place is quiet, and then I hear my name like somebody is standing right there with me, and I’ll look around, check the door, turn down any noise, just trying to see where it came from.

And when it’s that thing about my work being judged, that really gets in my head. It makes me nervous, and I start paying attention to everything I’m doing, like I’m being watched or evaluated somehow. So, no, they’re not giving me instructions exactly, but they do influence me because I react to them. I can’t just ignore it when it sounds that clear.
Do you ever find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or organized when these voices are happening?

Yes… yes, that’s actually one of the hardest parts. When the voices start, it’s like my mind doesn’t stay on one track. I’ll try to focus on something simple, but then my thoughts start running so fast I can’t catch them.

Like one minute I’m thinking about a client’s medicine, and then suddenly I’m thinking about my rent, and then a painting title I was considering, and then some line in a song feels like it has a message in it, and I’m trying to figure out what it means. It jumps like that—client, rent, painting, song, back to the voice, then wondering if I missed something important—and I can’t slow it down enough to make sense of it.

It’s not just being distracted. It feels crowded in my head, like everything is moving too quick, and I’m trying to organize it but it keeps slipping away from me. That’s when I get really upset, because I know I need to think clearly, especially with work things, but my mind won’t settle.
Do you find yourself doing things that don't make sense to you, or having trouble completing tasks because of these thoughts and voices?

Yes… yes, that does happen, and I feel embarrassed saying it because afterward I’ll think, “Why did I do that? That didn’t make any sense.” It’s not always like I’m choosing it on purpose. It’s more like I get stuck on something and can’t move forward.

There have been times when I’m on a client visit, and I’m supposed to be doing the regular things, you know, helping with what needs to be done, keeping track of the medicine cups or supplies, and then my mind will get all tangled up with the voices or the feeling that something is being watched or judged. And instead of finishing what I’m there to do, I’ll start arranging things. Like I’ll line up gloves, pill cups, even little crochet scraps if I have them with me, and I’ll put them into patterns, like they have to be in a certain order before I can keep going.

And it sounds strange saying it out loud, but in the moment it feels important, like I’m waiting for something to make sense. There have been times I’ve just stood in the hallway too, not doing anything, just staring, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal or cue to tell me what comes next. Then later I realize I lost time and didn’t finish the task the way I was supposed to, and I get upset with myself because I know it looks odd.
When your thoughts are jumping around like that, do you find that you're having trouble expressing them in a way that makes sense to others?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I know I feel like I’m not making sense in my own head when everything is jumping around, but I don’t always know how it sounds to somebody else.

Sometimes I’ll start explaining something and then I can hear myself taking too long, like I’m going around the block before I get to the point. I’ll say one thing, then I feel like I have to explain the thing behind that, and then there’s another piece connected to it, and by then I forget what the original question was. But I don’t know if that means I’m not making sense, or if I’m just overexplaining because I’m trying so hard to be clear.

People don’t always tell me, “you’re not making sense,” so I can’t say that for sure. I do notice I get frustrated because what I’m trying to say feels clear for a second, and then it sort of slips away while I’m talking. Then I’ll stop and say, “wait, what was I saying?” or I’ll have to back up. So… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really know. I just know it feels hard to get it out right when my mind is moving too fast.
Do you find that you're doing things in a way that seems unusual or out of character for you when these voices are happening?

Yes… yes, I think so. It feels very out of character for me, because I’m usually someone who knows what I’m supposed to be doing when I’m working. I take that seriously. But when the voices are happening, I can kind of get pulled off into something that doesn’t make sense.

Like I said, on client visits there have been times where I’m supposed to be doing the normal task, and instead I’ll just stop. I’ll start lining up gloves or pill cups, or even little crochet scraps if I have them with me, putting them in patterns like they have to be a certain way before I can move on. In the moment it feels like there’s a reason, like I’m trying to get something to line up right or I’m waiting for it to tell me what comes next.

And then other times I’ve just stood in the hallway staring. Not really doing anything. Just standing there like I’m waiting for some kind of signal or cue before I can keep going. Afterward, I know that must look strange, and it bothers me because that’s not how I want to act, especially at work. It doesn’t feel like my normal self.
Do you find that your daily activities or routines have become disorganized or harder to manage since the voices started?

Yes… it has. It’s gotten a lot harder to keep things straight day to day. I used to have a routine with my aide work, like I knew where I was supposed to be, what notes I had to write, what each visit needed, and even if it was tiring, I could manage it. But after the voices started getting worse, everything felt like it got scattered.

I missed shifts, which I’m ashamed to say, because I don’t like being unreliable. Sometimes I would think I had the time right or I’d get so caught up trying to get myself together that I’d lose track, and then it would be too late. And my care notes… I started mixing them up, like writing things in the wrong place or not keeping the visits organized the way I used to. That scared me because that job matters, and I got to the point where I felt like my job was in danger. Like people were noticing I wasn’t keeping up.

And outside of work, I stopped doing the things that used to help me feel normal. I used to go to my walking club, and I liked going to the library for the art talks. It gave me somewhere to be, people to see, something simple and steady. But I stopped going. I kept telling myself I’d go next time, or when I felt more together, but then I just stayed home. So most of the time I was alone at home, and my days didn’t really have shape anymore. It’s like everything got harder to organize, even the normal things.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when the voices are happening?

Yes… disconnected, or maybe too connected in a way that doesn’t make sense. It’s like they don’t stay in one line. One second I’m thinking about something I’m supposed to do, like a client’s medicine, and then before I can even finish that thought, my mind jumps to rent, like whether I paid it or how I’m going to manage it, and then suddenly I’m thinking of a painting title, like something I saw or wanted to name, and then there’s a song in the background and I’m wondering if there’s some kind of message in the words.

And it happens so fast that I can’t slow it down enough to sort it out. It’s not like I’m choosing to change subjects. It’s more like my thoughts are running ahead of me, and I’m trying to catch up, but by the time I grab one, another one has already started. So they feel disconnected because they don’t follow a normal path, but in the moment they also feel like they’re all somehow linked, even if I can’t explain why.

That’s the part that scares me or frustrates me, because I’ll try to make sense of it and I can’t. It’s just too fast.
Do you find yourself engaging in behaviors that seem irrational or without a clear purpose when the voices are not telling you to do something specific?

Yes… yes, I think so. Even when it’s not like the voices are giving me a clear instruction, I’ll still do things that don’t really have a purpose, or at least I can’t explain the purpose afterward.

Like on client visits, I’ll be there to do what I’m supposed to do, and then I’ll just stop in the middle of it. I might start taking gloves or pill cups and lining them up, moving them around into little patterns, almost like they have to sit a certain way. Sometimes I’ve had crochet scraps with me too, and I’ll do it with those, like arranging the colors or the pieces. In the moment it feels important, like I’m trying to make something settle or line up right, but it’s not part of the visit, it’s not helping the client, and later I look back and think, why was I doing that?

And there have been times I just stand there in the hallway, not really going anywhere or doing anything, just staring. It’s like I’m waiting for some signal or some feeling that tells me it’s okay to move again. But there isn’t a clear reason. I know that must look strange, and it embarrasses me, because I don’t want to be acting that way at work. It feels like I get stuck in something that doesn’t make sense.
Do you find it hard to express your thoughts in a logical and coherent way when you're hearing the voices?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean… I know sometimes when the voices are going on, it’s harder for me to talk the way I want to, because I’m trying to listen to you and also not listen to them, if that makes sense. But I don’t always know if I sound illogical, because in my head I’m trying to explain it right.

Sometimes I’ll start saying something and then I feel like I have to back up and explain the part before it, and then there’s another part connected to that, so I end up taking a long way around. I can hear myself doing it sometimes, like I’m giving too much detail or I’m not getting to the point fast enough, and then I get embarrassed and try to fix it, but fixing it makes me say even more.

So… I don’t know if it’s “not coherent,” exactly. People might have to ask me to repeat myself or slow down, but I’m not always aware in the moment. I just know it feels harder to get the thought out clean, like the words don’t come in the same order I need them to.
Do you feel like the voices are affecting your relationships with others or your ability to work?

Yes. It’s affected both, honestly. Work is the biggest thing, because I’ve always tried to be dependable as an aide, you know, like people are counting on me to come when I’m supposed to and keep things straight. But it got to the point where my job was in danger. I was missing shifts, or I’d get mixed up about visits, and then the care notes… I’d write them wrong or forget what I meant to put, or things wouldn’t be organized the way they used to be.

I used to have a way I did everything, like keeping track of who needed what and what I had already done, and when the voices are happening or even when I’m still shaken up from them, I can’t hold it all in order. Then I’m worried I’m going to make a mistake, and that makes me slower, and then I fall behind more. It’s embarrassing because this is my work, and I don’t want people thinking I don’t care. I do care. I just can’t always keep the visits organized like I used to.

And with people outside work… I pulled away a lot. I stopped going to my walking club, and I used to like that because it got me out and I could just be around people without it being too much. I also stopped going to the library art talks, and I really liked those. I’d tell myself I was just tired or I’d go next time, but then I just kept staying home. So I ended up mostly alone at home, and that probably made everything worse, but it felt easier than trying to be around people and keep myself together.
Do you feel like the voices are causing you significant distress or interfering with your daily life and relationships?

Yes… very much. It’s not just upsetting in the moment, it’s like it spills over into everything I’m supposed to be doing.

With my aide job, I got to the point where I was scared I was going to lose it. I was missing shifts, and then when I did go, I’d get mixed up with the care notes or not keep the visits straight the way I used to. I used to be more organized with that, like I knew what needed to be done and what I had already written down, but then it started feeling like I couldn’t hold it all together. And that made me feel ashamed, because people are depending on me.

And then outside of work, I kind of stopped doing the things that kept me connected. I stopped going to my walking club, and I stopped going to the library art talks. Those were things I actually liked, but I just kept staying home instead. So then I was mostly alone at home, and that made me feel even more cut off. So yes, it’s interfering a lot.
Have you ever felt like the voices or your thoughts were so real that you questioned what was real and what wasn't?

Yes… that’s part of why I came in, honestly. Because when it happens, it doesn’t feel like just a thought in my head. It sounds clear, like somebody is right there in my little studio with me, saying my name. I’ll be sitting there and the house is quiet, nobody’s there, but I hear it like it’s in the room.

And then when they say things about my work being judged, that really gets to me, because it feels like it’s not just me worrying. It feels like I’m being told it, like it’s happening. So I start looking around or listening harder, trying to figure out if someone is actually there or if maybe I missed something. I know that probably sounds strange, but in the moment it’s very hard to separate it, because it’s so clear.

Afterward I can think, “Okay, nobody was in here,” but when it’s happening, yes, I question what’s real. It scares me because I don’t want to be confused like that, but that’s how real the voices can feel.
Have you ever felt like you were in a different world or reality when the voices were happening?

I don’t know if I’d call it a whole different world exactly, but when the voices are happening, it feels like the room changes for me. Like I’m sitting in my little studio and it’s quiet, and I know nobody should be there, but then I hear somebody say my name so clear that it feels like someone is standing right there with me.

And when they start saying my work is being judged, it’s like I get pulled into that being true. Not like a dream or anything, but like this other version of what’s happening where I’m not just home alone anymore — I’m being watched or evaluated somehow. I’ll look around, listen, try to figure out where it came from, because it doesn’t feel like just a thought. It feels real in the room.

So maybe not a different world like I’m somewhere else, but a different reality in that moment, yes. Because the quiet house doesn’t feel quiet anymore. It feels like there’s someone there, saying my name, judging me, and I have to sort out whether it’s real or not.
Do you find it hard to stick to one topic when you're talking to someone?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try to answer what somebody asked me, but my mind jumps ahead or sideways before I can finish the one thing.

Like I’ll be talking about one of my clients and their medicine, and then suddenly I’m thinking about my rent being due, and then for some reason I’m thinking about a painting title from one of the art talks, and then a song I heard earlier will pop in and I’ll start wondering if there was some message in it. It all comes so fast that I can’t slow it down enough to make it come out in a straight line.

So when I’m talking to someone, I might start on one topic and then I’m on another one before I even realize I switched. Sometimes I can see the other person looking confused, and then I get embarrassed and try to go back, but by then there’s already three or four other things running through my head. It feels like I’m chasing my own thoughts instead of just having a conversation.
Do you often find it hard to keep your thoughts in order when you're not hearing the voices?

Yes, even when I’m not hearing anything, my thoughts still get… tangled, I guess. It’s like they don’t line up right. They run so fast that I can’t keep them in order.

I’ll be trying to think about one simple thing, like a client’s medicine or what I need to do for work, and then before I even finish that thought I’m on rent, and then some title of a painting from an art talk will pop in, and then a song I heard earlier starts playing in my head and I’m wondering if there was some message in it. It’s not like I sit down and choose to think about all that. It just takes off.

And then I’m trying to make sense of it all at once, but it’s too fast. Like there’s no pause between one thought and the next. I’ll try to slow myself down and say, “Okay, just think about the first thing,” but then I’ve already jumped to something else. It makes it hard to explain myself because by the time I start talking, I’ve lost the order of what I meant to say.

So yes, the voices make it worse in a different way, but even without them, my thoughts can be racing so much that I can’t get them to settle into a straight line.
Do you find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner when you're not hearing the voices?

Yes, I do. Even when the voices aren’t there, I still have a hard time getting it to come out right. In my head it feels like everything is moving too fast, like I’ll start with one thought and before I can finish saying it, another one has already shoved in front of it.

Like, I might be trying to explain something simple about a client’s medicine, and then suddenly I’m thinking about my rent, and then my mind jumps to some painting title I heard, and then a song comes into my head and I’m wondering if there was some message in it. And I know that sounds like a lot all at once, but that’s how it feels — like one thing keeps setting off the next thing, and I can’t slow it down enough to put it in order.

So when I try to talk, I’ll start in one place and then I hear myself going somewhere else, and I can tell it probably doesn’t make sense to the person listening. I’ll try to back up and explain, but then I lose what I was originally trying to say. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be confusing. I know what I mean for a second, and then it gets all mixed up before I can get it out clearly.
Do you ever use words or phrases that you know others might not understand, or make up new words when you're talking?

I don’t think I really make up words, no. Not on purpose, anyway. I mean, sometimes I might use a phrase that makes sense to me in the moment, and then someone looks at me like they don’t know what I mean, but I’m not sitting there inventing a whole new word or anything.

Sometimes I’ll describe something in my own way because I can’t find the right regular word fast enough, like I’m trying to get the feeling across, but I don’t know if that counts. I might say something comes out “twisted” or “stacked up” or “too loud in my head,” things like that, but those are real words, just maybe not the way other people would say it.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed myself making up new words. If I do say something confusing, I think it’s more because I’m not explaining it right than because I’m using words nobody has ever heard before.
Have you ever had a period where these voices and disorganized thoughts lasted for a short time, like a few days or a week, and then stopped?

No, it hasn’t really been like just a few days or a week and then gone. I wish it was like that. The voices and those thoughts about my work being watched… that’s been going on for a long time now, like about nine months.

It might change some from day to day, like some days it feels louder or harder to push aside, and some days I can sort of get through what I have to do, but it doesn’t just stop. It’s not like I had one short spell and then everything cleared up. It keeps coming back, and the fear about people watching what I’m doing at work has stayed with me too. It feels fixed there, like I keep trying to talk myself out of it, but it doesn’t really leave. So, no… not a short time. More like months.

There have been times I’ve just stood in the hallway too, not doing anything, just staring, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal or cue to tell me what comes next. Then later I realize I lost time and didn’t finish the task the way I was supposed to, and I get upset with myself because I know it looks odd.

patient.answer:

But I don’t know if that means I’m not making sense, or if I’m just overexplaining because I’m trying so hard to be clear.

People don’t always tell me, “you’re not making sense,” so I can’t say that for sure. I do notice I get frustrated because what I’m trying to say feels clear for a second, and then it sort of slips away while I’m talking. Yes… it has. It’s gotten a lot harder to keep things straight day to day. I used to have a routine with my aide work, like I knew where I was supposed to be, what notes I had to write, what each visit needed, and even if it was tiring, I could manage it. I missed shifts, which I’m ashamed to say, because I don’t like being unreliable. Sometimes I would think I had the time right or I’d get so caught up trying to get myself together that I’d lose track, and then it would be too late. And my care notes… I started mixing them up, like writing things in the wrong place or not keeping the visits organized the way I used to. That scared me because that job matters, and I got to the point where I felt like my job was in danger. Like people were noticing I wasn’t keeping up.

And outside of work, I stopped doing the things that used to help me feel normal. I used to go to my walking club, and I liked going to the library for the art talks. It gave me somewhere to be, people to see, something simple and steady. But I stopped going. I kept telling myself I’d go next time, or when I felt more together, but then I just stayed home. doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences disorganized thinking as part of their symptoms

Yes… disconnected, or maybe too connected in a way that doesn’t make sense. It’s like they don’t stay in one line. One second I’m thinking about something I’m supposed to do, like a client’s medicine, and then before I can even finish that thought, my mind jumps to rent, like whether I paid it or how I’m going to manage it, and then suddenly I’m thinking of a painting title, like something I saw or wanted to name, and then there’s a song in the background and I’m wondering if there’s some kind of message in the words.

And it happens so fast that I can’t slow it down enough to sort it out. It’s not like I’m choosing to change subjects. It’s more like my thoughts are running ahead of me, and I’m trying to catch up, but by the time I grab one, another one has already started. So they feel disconnected because they don’t follow a normal path, but in the moment they also feel like they’re all somehow linked, even if I can’t explain why.

That’s the part that scares me or frustrates me, because I’ll try to make sense of it and I can’t. It’s just too fast.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences disorganized thinking as part of their symptoms

patient.answer:
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Sometimes I’ll start saying something and then I feel like I have to back up and explain the part before it, and then there’s another part connected to that, so I end up taking a long way around. I can hear myself doing it sometimes, like I’m giving too much detail or I’m not getting to the point fast enough, and then I get embarrassed and try to fix it, but fixing it makes me say even more.

So… I don’t know if it’s “not coherent,” exactly. People might have to ask me to repeat myself or slow down, but I’m not always aware in the moment. I just know it feels harder to get the thought out clean, like the words don’t come in the same order I need them to.

Yes. It’s affected both, honestly. I used to have a way I did everything, like keeping track of who needed what and what I had already done, and when the voices are happening or even when I’m still shaken up from them, I can’t hold it all in order. Then I’m worried I’m going to make a mistake, and that makes me slower, and then I fall behind more. It’s embarrassing because this is my work, and I don’t want people thinking I don’t care. doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant break from reality

It sounds clear, like somebody is right there in my little studio with me, saying my name. I’ll be sitting there and the house is quiet, nobody’s there, but I hear it like it’s in the room.

And then when they say things about my work being judged, that really gets to me, because it feels like it’s not just me worrying. It feels like I’m being told it, like it’s happening. So I start looking around or listening harder, trying to figure out if someone is actually there or if maybe I missed something. I know that probably sounds strange, but in the moment it’s very hard to separate it, because it’s so clear.

Afterward I can think, “Okay, nobody was in here,” but when it’s happening, yes, I question what’s real. It scares me because I don’t want to be confused like that, but that’s how real the voices can feel.

And when they start saying my work is being judged, it’s like I get pulled into that being true. Yes… I do. I mean, I try to answer what somebody asked me, but my mind jumps ahead or sideways before I can finish the one thing.

Yes, even when I’m not hearing anything, my thoughts still get… tangled, I guess. It’s like they don’t line up right. They run so fast that I can’t keep them in order.

I’ll be trying to think about one simple thing, like a client’s medicine or what I need to do for work, and then before I even finish that thought I’m on rent, and then some title of a painting from an art talk will pop in, and then a song I heard earlier starts playing in my head and I’m wondering if there was some message in it. It’s not like I sit down and choose to think about all that. It just takes off.

And then I’m trying to make sense of it all at once, but it’s too fast. Like there’s no pause between one thought and the next. I’ll try to slow myself down and say, “Okay, just think about the first thing,” but then I’ve already jumped to something else. It makes it hard to explain myself because by the time I start talking, I’ve lost the order of what I meant to say.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking and speech
doctor.question: Do you find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner when you're not hearing the voices?

target_item.name: Racing_Thoughts

patient.answer:
Yes, I do. Even when the voices aren’t there, I still have a hard time getting it to come out right. In my head it feels like everything is moving too fast, like I’ll start with one thought and before I can finish saying it, another one has already shoved in front of it.

Like, I might be trying to explain something simple about a client’s medicine, and then suddenly I’m thinking about my rent, and then my mind jumps to some painting title I heard, and then a song comes into my head and I’m wondering if there was some message in it. And I know that sounds like a lot all at once, but that’s how it feels — like one thing keeps setting off the next thing, and I can’t slow it down enough to put it in order.

So when I try to talk, I’ll start in one place and then I hear myself going somewhere else, and I can tell it probably doesn’t make sense to the person listening. I’ll try to back up and explain, but then I lose what I was originally trying to say. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be confusing. I know what I mean for a second, and then it gets all mixed up before I can get it out clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for disorganized thinking and speech, which is a key feature of schizophrenia spectrum disorders, by asking about the presence of neologisms

patient.answer:
I don’t think I really make up words, no. Not on purpose, anyway. I mean, sometimes I might use a phrase that makes sense to me in the moment, and then someone looks at me like they don’t know what I mean, but I’m not sitting there inventing a whole new word or anything.

Sometimes I’ll describe something in my own way because I can’t find the right regular word fast enough, like I’m trying to get the feeling across, but I don’t know if that counts. I might say something comes out “twisted” or “stacked up” or “too loud in my head,” things like that, but those are real words, just maybe not the way other people would say it.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed myself making up new words. If I do say something confusing, I think it’s more because I’m not explaining it right than because I’m using words nobody has ever heard before.
